title: Compose rewrites dollar signs in values, so file bytes and resolved value can differ
summary: Compose changes some bytes of a value before using it: $$ becomes one literal dollar sign in a Compose file, and in an env_file the same line is read in one of two modes (default parsing with interpolation of unquoted and double-quoted values, or format: raw, which keeps quotes and dollar signs as written), with the mode declared in the referencing Compose file, not in the env file.
rationale: For a secret that contains a dollar sign, the bytes in the file are not the value Compose passes on: $$ shrinks to $, and under default env_file parsing a $NAME inside an unquoted or double-quoted value is replaced by the variable's value or an empty string with a warning. Whether the same env file text is the credential, a reference mixed with part of one, or a different string depends on the parse mode written in another file, which a reader of the env file alone does not have. No Docker page states whether $$ is also an escape inside an env file. The expectation cannot be asserted from the pages read: which source span stands for the secret, and whether a reader must map source bytes to the resolved value, is an unsettled question for consumers. Handoff: decoded-source mapping and resolution preconditions belong to the representation contract owned by #150 and credential-eval; no fixture is added here because a value that needs a dollar sign inside it would have to be invented for a family whose grammar does not allow one.

expectation.rationale: Not assertable. Docker documents the rewriting rules (a $$ stands for a literal dollar sign; unquoted and double-quoted env file values have interpolation applied; single-quoted values are literal; format: raw passes values as-is, including quotes and $ signs), but no page settles how a source span maps to the resolved secret, and no page states $$ handling inside an env file. What would settle it: a documented decision by the consumer contract (#150 / credential-eval) on source-span coverage for rewritten values, and a Docker statement or a captured Compose behaviour on $$ in env files.

sources.supports: You can use a $$ (double-dollar sign) when your configuration needs a literal dollar sign. This also prevents Compose from interpolating a value.

format: raw (Docker Compose 2.30.0 and later) lets you use an env_file with key=value items, but without any attempt from Compose to parse the value for interpolation. This lets you pass values as-is, including quotes and $ signs. When not set, env_file is parsed according to the Compose rules outlined in Env_file format.
Unquoted and double-quoted (") values have Interpolation applied. Single-quoted (') values are used literally.
--no-interpolate: Don't interpolate environment variables. --no-env-resolution: Don't resolve service env files.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04. Origin: evidence-derived; no fixture, so no synthetic value. The Compose version boundary for format: raw (2.30.0) and for required: false (2.24.0) is documented on the services page; behaviour of older versions is not claimed.
